messages:
anya: Hey team — customer (org: acme-edu) reports they hit 0 credits at 23:58 local and then saw quota restore at 00:45, causing a ~47m outage window. They insist their tenant is set to 'monthly reset at midnight local' in the console. Can billing confirm how reset time is computed?

mike: Copying logs from the customer: they hit 429s with Retry-After: 600. Their header shows `X-Org-Timezone: America/Chicago` and `X-Request-ID: r-3f9a2b`. They claim dashboard still showed 0/1000 credits at 00:10.

billing-ops: Quick note: console display and actual backend refill can be out-of-sync if the refill job runs in a different region. We normally run the replenish batch at 00:00 UTC by default unless an org has explicit timezone-anchored reset. Does this org have the TZ override set?

anya: The customer said they configured "reset at local midnight" via the org settings but we couldn't repro in our account. I asked for a screenshot, they attached one showing the UI toggle enabled and a ledger export with last refill timestamp `2024-03-24T05:00:00Z`. That looks like 00:00 CDT converted.

sre-oncall: Two angles: 1) if the replenish job was delayed due to a backlog or job runner failover it could move past the visible UI change but backend would still mark credits as available once the job completes. 2) If there was a migration/rollout of the billing scheduler around that time we might have had jobs run on a different instance with stale cache. I'll check runner logs.

support-bot: Incident detection: Billing refill job latency spike detected ~1708600100 (alert id: refill-latency-prod).

mike: Repro steps from customer (sanitized):
```
# hit token limit
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"x"}'
# returns 429
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 600
X-Request-ID: r-3f9a2b
```
Then at 00:45 they retried and got 200.

anya: Can billing-ops confirm whether the org reset schedule is stored as an absolute UTC time or as a timezone-aware rule? If stored as a cron in UTC then DST shifts might surface. Customer is in CDT (DST active).

billing-ops: We store a rule like `TZ=America/Chicago; hour=0; minute=0` which then gets converted to UTC at evaluation time. DST should be handled by the timezone library. However, there was a deploy last week that changed the scheduling library from pytz to zoneinfo on some hosts — there were a few discrepant offsets during rollout. That could explain a one-off misfire.

anya: Ok — that matches the customer's timeline. Could that rollout also cause the UI toggle to show 'enabled' while the backend scheduled job was still registered with previous semantics?

billing-ops: Possible. If the toggle flips a DB flag but the scheduler caches the rule, we'd need a cache invalidation to propagate. I can grep memoized keys.

sre-oncall: Checked the scheduler logs: around 1708600000 one instance reported `failed to load zoneinfo` and retried, delaying the enqueue by ~30m. I can attach logs.

anya: Customer-facing line: acknowledge they hit a refill delay caused by a scheduler rollout, apologize, and offer to top up the missing minutes if they want immediate remediation. Also propose plan: run a backfill to re-enqueue any missed refill events and add a one-time customer credit.

mike: Customer asked about long-term mitigation — they want guarantees around burst windows. Suggested actions: 1) make refill job idempotent and tolerant to transient zone library errors, 2) add a metric for 'refill-lag' to alert earlier, 3) show last successful refill timestamp on org settings page (so customers can see exact UTC/converted time).

billing-ops: Agreed. I'll open a PR to invalidate scheduler caches on toggle and add zoneinfo fallback. We'll also add an event in the billing audit log (refill_attempt/refill_succeeded).

support-bot: Ticket created: #SUP-4821 (customer: acme-edu) — billing-ops will propose remediation & offer credit.

anya: For SRE: can you check if any other orgs hit refill-latency alert in the same 2h window? If it's widespread we need a postmortem.

sre-oncall: Running quick query — found 7 orgs with refill-latency > 15m between 1708599000 and 1708605000. I'll escalate to incidents if >10.

mike: Final ask before I reply to customer: billing-ops confirm whether the ledger export timestamp `2024-03-24T05:00:00Z` should be interpreted as 'refill processed at that moment' vs 'refill scheduled for that moment but processed later'. Need exact semantics so we can explain.

billing-ops: That timestamp is the actual processed time. UI might show the scheduled/target local time, which is confusing — we'll update the UI copy.

anya: Great. I'll send a reply: short explanation, apology, top-up offer, and status of fixes (cache invalidation + zoneinfo fallback + new metrics + UI timestamp clarification). :white_check_mark:

mike: Thanks all. I'll paste the customer message once it's sent.

support-bot: Reminder: set SLO impact tag and link to PRs in the ticket when done.
